## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Āvaṭṭahāravibhaṅga* ("Conveying a Conversion: Analysis") is an analytical section of the *Nettippakaraṇa* (Ne 10), categorized within the paracanonical or late Khuddaka collections of the Pali Tipiṭaka. It constitutes an exposition (*vibhaṅga*) of *āvaṭṭa-hāra* ("the mode of conveying a conversion"), one of the sixteen interpretive methods (*hāra*) designed by the *Netti* for structuring, analyzing, and explaining canonical Dhamma discourses.

 Other major Pali reuse partners include the *Pāyāsi Sutta* (DN 23), *Nidāna Saṁyutta* (SN 12), *Assalāyana Sutta* (MN 93), *Mahākammavibhaṅga Sutta* (MN 136), the *Peṭakopadesa* (Pe 8), and various nipātas of the *Aṅguttara Nikāya* (AN 3, AN 4, AN 7, AN 10) [DharmaNexus]. Text reuse is likewise substantial in the commentarial literature, specifically the *Nettippakaraṇa-aṭṭhakathā* and the sub-commentary *Nettivibhāvinī* [DharmaNexus]. Cross-language alignments computed by DharmaNexus include matches with the Sanskrit *Pratītyasamutpādādivibhaṅganirdeśasūtra*, Tibetan translations such as the *Bodhisattvapiṭaka* and *Saddharmānusmṛtyupasthāna*, and the Chinese *Ekottarika Āgama* (T 125) [DharmaNexus].

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on catalog and DharmaNexus data.*
